bugs.error_message: Red-team QA (device-local web build): after a real payment + void on a table check, Receipts (Kasovi belejki) and Analitika (Отчети) both show '0 results / not available' instead of the data, even though the paid+voided ticket is verifiably persisted in localStorage history-storage.
bugs.root_cause: Deeper root cause found during fix: this is NOT a missing fallback, it's two separate, incompatible data architectures. The order/table/payment/void flow tested (TableDetailScreen) runs on legacy zustand stores (orderStore/historyStore, localStorage 'history-storage') used only for the pre-cloud onboarding sandbox. HistoryScreen and AnalyticsScreen were already migrated to the new domain-driven useOrderiaData() layer, which is cloud-only by design; local_only mode there is for an offline-but-paired device, not for the legacy sandbox. The two never merge automatically — migration from legacy to cloud is an explicit one-time JSON-file import (src/features/legacy-migration, Settings screen), not a live read path. Merging historyStore reads into these screens would conflate two incompatible data models and was judged out of scope for a safe fix. What WAS a real, fixable bug: both screens blamed 'internet required' even when mode !== 'cloud' on a device that has real internet (sync.online true) — factually misleading, since the actual blocker is 'not connected to a cloud business yet', unrelated to connectivity.
bugs.fix: Fixed the misleading-message bug: src/screens/HistoryScreen.tsx and src/screens/AnalyticsScreen.tsx now distinguish mode !== 'cloud' (shows new copy.cloudRequired, pointing to Settings) from sync.online === false (shows the original copy.onlineRequired) in tr/bg/en. Added regression tests (AnalyticsScreen.test.tsx, HistoryScreen.test.tsx) asserting the two states render distinct copy. Did NOT attempt to surface legacy sandbox data in these screens — see root_cause for why that was scoped out. tsc/lint/full jest (64 suites, 319 tests) all pass.

Note: unlike Receipts/Analytics, MenuScreen and AddMenuItemScreen already had a working legacy-store fallback for browsing/adding menu items in local mode - only the AI-draft feature is genuinely cloud-only (calls an OpenAI/NVIDIA-backed Supabase edge function), so no local fallback was attempted there, only the message fix. bugs.error_message: Red-team QA (QR ordering / customer-facing flow): the entire 'QR Menu' feature (Settings > QR Menu, toggle 'Allow direct ordering' ON by default) is a fake implementation - a manager can generate and print/share a QR code per table that customers would scan, but nothing behind it works.
bugs.root_cause: getMenuUrl() builds a URL to a hardcoded, non-configurable domain (https://orderia-menu.app/menu/{tableId}) with no settings UI to change it and no env var. That domain has no relationship to this codebase: AppNavigator.tsx has no React Navigation `linking` config at all, so even if that domain pointed at this app's own web deployment there is no route handler for /menu/:tableId. The QR image itself is generated by sending the URL to a third-party service (api.qrserver.com) instead of the react-native-qrcode-svg package that's imported for it. validateQRAccess/getQRMenuData exist and look plausible but are never called by anything reachable from outside the app's own JS runtime - there is no server endpoint anywhere to receive a scan. addTicketLine is imported specifically to receive guest orders and is never invoked. A customer scanning a real printed QR code from this feature hits a dead/unrelated domain with zero indication anything is wrong.
bugs.fix: Per explicit user decision (asked directly, not assumed): disabled/hid the feature rather than building the real guest-ordering flow (a substantial new feature: public web page + order-ingestion endpoint) or leaving it silently broken. Removed the only entry point - the 'QR Menu' ServiceListRow in SettingsScreen.tsx (Yönetim/management section) that navigated to QRMenuScreenModern. The QRMenu route registration, QRMenuScreenModern, and QRMenuContext.tsx were left in place (not deleted, per user's global 'prefer edit over delete' rule) - they are simply unreachable from any UI now. tsc/lint/full jest (65 suites, 323 tests) all pass; verified live that no 'QR' text/entry remains anywhere in the Settings screen.

Confirmed via DOM measurement: the chip button was 48px tall but its ScrollView wrapper measured 264px. After centering, the compact pill row just floats centered inside that oversized box instead of stretching to fill it -- same underlying bug, different visual symptom.

DOM re-measurement after the fix: wrapper shrank from 264px to 72px, matching content height.

bugs.error_message: User-reported: tapping 'Take payment' on Home always shows 'No tables in this hall yet / Ask your manager to configure the table layout', even though Home's own dashboard shows open tables with an unpaid balance
bugs.root_cause: filterShiftBoardTables's scope==='payment' required table.state === 'payment_pending'. That derived state only becomes true when a check already has a partial payment recorded (checks.some(c=>c.status==='partially_paid')) -- no code path in the app ever sets tableSession.status to 'payment_pending' directly. A fully-unpaid open table (the overwhelmingly common case for this button) never matched, so the quick action was effectively dead for its primary use case. Home's own 'Payment due' stat and quick-action badge already used the correct definition (remainingMinor > 0), so the two screens disagreed.
bugs.fix: Changed the payment scope check to table.remainingMinor <= 0 (excluded) instead of table.state !== 'payment_pending', matching HomeScreen's existing definition. Updated the existing shiftBoardModel test that had locked in the old (buggy) exclusion behavior, and added an explicit assertion for the zero-balance boundary. Also split OrdersFlowScreen's empty-state message: a scope filter matching zero tables now shows 'No tables match these filters' instead of the misleading 'ask your manager to configure the table layout', which only fits a genuinely hall-less scenario.

bugs.fix: Lazily initialize installDismissed from window.localStorage (web-only, guarded by Platform.OS==='web'), and write the flag on both dismiss paths (the X icon and the 'Later' button). Deliberately scoped to the install prompt only -- the separate update-ready banner (updateDeferred) is left session-only, since re-prompting about a pending update on next load is correct behavior, unlike repeatedly begging to install.

bugs.error_message: P0: 'Workspace unavailable' shown to every account after the first, when signing in/up on a browser that already has a registered device from a different account -- register_device RPC returns 403 device_scope_mismatch, and 'Try again' retries forever with no recovery UI
bugs.root_cause: getOrCreateDeviceId() persists a single global AsyncStorage/localStorage key ('orderia.cloud.device_id') shared by the whole browser install, never scoped per-user and never cleared on sign-out. The server's register_device RPC (supabase/migrations/20260726160000_auth_tenancy.sql:280-348) does `insert ... on conflict (id) do update ... where user_id = auth.uid() and organization_id = X and branch_id = Y` -- if that device id already has a row from a DIFFERENT user/org, the WHERE excludes it, zero rows update, and the function raises 42501 device_scope_mismatch. Confirmed via live QA: created a manager account (new org), then signed up a waiter account and joined the same org via restaurant code -- second account hit this immediately and permanently, on both signUp and signIn paths.
bugs.fix: FIXED (option A, user-approved): activateBranch() now wraps registerDevice() in a try/catch; on device_scope_mismatch it calls a new regenerateDeviceId() (overwrites the stored id with a fresh uuid) and retries registerDevice() once. A second failure propagates normally instead of looping. Verified live end-to-end: signed manager out, signed waiter in with no manual localStorage clearing -- succeeded automatically, device id changed from da337697... to db76768e..., repeated a second switch back to the manager with the same result.

bugs.error_message: P3: minor copy/locale defects found during manager+waiter QA pass
bugs.root_cause: (a) Workspace-unavailable error screen shows an English title but a Turkish body ('Orderia calisma alaniniz yuklenemedi') regardless of selected language -- likely a hardcoded fallback string bypassing the i18n system entirely. (b) Add Table screen's helper text leaks an unresolved template placeholder literally: 'If left empty, "Table {seq}" will be used'. (c) Table status pill renders 'AVAILABLE' with a Turkish dotted-I ('AVAİLABLE') under English locale, a CSS text-transform/lang-attribute locale leak.
bugs.fix: FIXED. (a) Root cause was a real race: AuthContext stored resolved t.xxx strings in errorMessage state; if an error fired before LocalizationContext finished loading the persisted language from AsyncStorage (default 'tr' on first render), the resolved Turkish text got baked into state and never updated even after the language later hydrated to English. Replaced with an errorKey ('authWorkspaceLoadFailed' etc.) resolved live against the CURRENT t on every render, so the displayed text always matches the current language regardless of when the error fired. Dynamic helper-derived messages (signIn/signUp/onboarding) kept as direct text since those fire well after mount. (b) tableNameHint changed from a static string with a literal unresolved '{seq}' to a function (seq: number) => string, called with the real displayHall.nextTableSequence at the AddTableScreenModern call site -- verified live, hint now reads 'If left empty, "Table 2" will be used'. (c) Root cause was public/index.html's <html lang> never being templated (dead %LANG_ISO_CODE% placeholder) and never synced to the in-app language selection, so CSS text-transform:uppercase used the browser/OS locale's special-casing rules (Turkish dotted-I) regardless of the selected UI language. Set a sane static default (lang="tr", matching LocalizationContext's own default state) and added a useEffect in LocalizationContext.tsx that sets document.documentElement.lang = language on every language change (web-only). Verified live: document.documentElement.lang reads 'en' and 'AVAILABLE' renders correctly under English.

bugs.error_message: EAS Android build fails at Gradle: 'error: An organization ID or slug is required (provide with --org)' -- task :app:createBundleReleaseJsAndAssets_SentryUpload_... FAILED, whole build ERRORED (EAS_BUILD_UNKNOWN_GRADLE_ERROR)
bugs.root_cause: The @sentry/react-native Gradle plugin (sentry.gradle) runs a sourcemap-upload step during every release build via sentry-cli, and hard-fails the ENTIRE build if no Sentry org/project is configured. This project has never had real Sentry credentials set (confirmed by the build log's earlier warning: '[@sentry/react-native/expo] Missing config for organization, project') and none are set as EAS environment variables for any profile ('No environment variables ... found for the preview environment on EAS'). The web build already has an established, deliberate policy for this exact situation -- scripts/verify-release-env.mjs runs with --warn-only so a missing Sentry config warns but never blocks a release (see cerebrum.md decision log, 2026-08-07). The Android EAS build profiles never got the equivalent treatment, so it hard-blocked every APK/AAB build.
bugs.fix: Added "env": {"SENTRY_DISABLE_AUTO_UPLOAD": "true"} to all three eas.json build profiles (development, preview, production). This is the sentry.gradle plugin's own documented escape hatch (project.ext.shouldSentryAutoUploadGeneral checks exactly this env var) -- it skips the sourcemap upload task entirely rather than failing the build. No functional impact on the shipped app; only effect is Sentry won't have symbolicated stack traces until real org/project credentials are configured later.

bugs.error_message: EAS Android build fails at Kotlin compile: MainActivity.kt:2:1 'Syntax error: Expecting a top level declaration' and 'imports are only allowed in the beginning of file' (Task :app:compileReleaseKotlin FAILED)
bugs.root_cause: The committed native MainActivity.kt had 'import expo.modules.splashscreen.SplashScreenManager' as line 1, BEFORE the 'package com.zwolfe.orderia' declaration on line 2. Kotlin requires package to be the first statement in a file (before any imports). Likely caused by a prior expo-splashscreen config-plugin injection (marked '@generated begin expo-splashscreen ... DO NOT MODIFY') that prepended its import above the existing package line during a manual edit or partial prebuild sync, and it went unnoticed because this project builds from a committed android/ dir (not regenerated per-build) and had never been built via EAS before this session.
bugs.fix: Moved 'package com.zwolfe.orderia' to line 1, and moved 'import expo.modules.splashscreen.SplashScreenManager' down into the normal import block (after the other expo import), preserving all other imports and code untouched. Verified no other .kt/.java files under android/app/src/main/java/com/zwolfe/orderia/ have the same malformed import-before-package ordering.

bugs.error_message: User-reported: cannot add tables for new halls when creating them (add-table fails with an error, only works for the first hall)
bugs.root_cause: SupabaseLayoutGateway.load() computed 'nextTableSequence' PER HALL (max sequence_number among that hall's own tables + 1), so every newly created hall's first table always suggested sequence_number=1. But the DB has restaurant_tables_active_sequence_unique, a UNIQUE INDEX on (branch_id, sequence_number) -- i.e. sequence numbers are unique across the WHOLE branch, not per hall. Since hall #1 already owns sequence_number 1 (and usually more), inserting a table into any subsequent hall with the suggested sequence_number=1 hit a unique-constraint violation and the insert threw, surfaced to the user as a generic error on Add Table.
bugs.fix: Changed layoutGateway.ts load() to compute a single branch-wide max(sequence_number) across ALL tables (not grouped by hall_id), and assign that +1 as every hall's nextTableSequence -- matching the DB's branch-wide uniqueness. AddTableScreenModern already just reads displayHall.nextTableSequence for both the placeholder and the actual insert payload, so no screen changes were needed.

bugs.error_message: User asked: does the APK version have Supabase auth? Investigation found EVERY prior Android build (v2.0.0, v2.0.1) shipped with NO working Supabase auth/cloud sync at all -- silently fell back to local-only offline mode.
bugs.root_cause: EXPO_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL and EXPO_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY only existed in the local, gitignored .env file. EAS Build reads env vars from eas.json's per-profile 'env' block (which only had SENTRY_DISABLE_AUTO_UPLOAD) or from EAS's own project-level environment variable store -- confirmed via 'eas env:list' that NO environment (preview/production/development) had any variables configured. readSupabaseEnvironment() (src/config/environment.ts) returns null when both vars are absent, so getSupabaseClient() returned null and the whole app silently ran in local-only mode in every APK build. Verified directly by unzipping the built APK and grepping index.android.bundle for the project's actual Supabase URL substring -- zero matches, confirming the value was never injected at build time.
bugs.fix: Ran 'eas env:create' to add EXPO_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL and EXPO_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY (plaintext visibility -- these are public, RLS-protected client keys, same as what ships in the PWA) to both the preview and production EAS environments. Verified with 'eas env:list --environment preview'. Triggered a fresh Android build (75804e08) to pick them up.

bugs.error_message: User-reported on mobile (garbled): 'secure uuid is [un]available, i can[not] get payment' -- thrown while trying to take/confirm a payment
bugs.root_cause: defaultUuid() used globalThis.crypto?.randomUUID?.() and threw 'Secure UUID generation is unavailable' whenever that API was missing. crypto.randomUUID requires a secure context (HTTPS) and a reasonably modern engine; it is not reliably present in every Android WebView / PWA context this app runs in, and the project ships no crypto polyfill. This exact class of bug was already found and fixed once before in workspaceFormat.ts (see its comment: 'projede crypto polyfil'i yok, dolayisiyla siparis gonderme yolunda patlama riski tasiyordu') by switching to react-native-uuid, which every other UUID call site in the codebase (orderCommands, checkSplitCommands, AuthContext, menuCatalogGateway) already uses -- paymentPlanner.ts was the one call site that was missed during that earlier fix.
bugs.fix: Replaced defaultUuid()'s body with String(uuid.v4()) using the same react-native-uuid import already used everywhere else, removing the crypto.randomUUID dependency and its throw entirely. Verified: tsc --noEmit clean, npx jest src/features/payments passes (9/9).

bugs.fix: Added localOnlySyncMode (persisted to AsyncStorage under 'orderia:localOnlySyncMode') and setLocalOnlySyncMode to OrderiaDataContext. When on, the three automatic sync triggers (mount/branch-change effect incl. realtime hint subscription, AppState-active listener, browser online-event listener) are gated off; refresh() itself is untouched, so manual sync and direct-RPC actions (payments, catalog, hall/table management) still work normally regardless of the toggle -- only the OutboxPushWorker/SyncPullEngine background cadence is paused. Local writes keep queuing in the existing offline outbox exactly as before. Added a Sync section to SettingsScreen (visible only in cloud mode) with the toggle and a 'Sync now' row showing pending-change count / last-synced time / offline state, calling refresh() on tap. Added a provider test asserting auto-push is skipped while the toggle is on and still fires on manual refresh. Full suite: 65/65 suites, 332/332 tests pass; tsc clean.
